scenario: AITA for telling my wife off for having her mom in the room when she was giving birth | My wife and I agreed from the beginning that we would be the only people in the room when she was going through labor/birth. Her mother and I also don’t get along very well, and neither of us wanted that stress the day of. There was an issue and I was late getting to the hospital, not by a ton though. There was still 3+ hours of labor until the baby came. However, by the time I got there, my wife had called her mother and told her to come. It caused a lot of tension and made the process pretty uncomfortable for me, and thus made it harder to support my wife. We didn’t get that special one on one time with the baby either (we initially planned on having a full day of just us, but it ended up only being a few hours) and I’m really upset about it. It’s been a few weeks and my wife asked me why I am so moody about the topic of the birth, and I exploded at her for violating the plan that we had from the beginning. She cried and blamed me for being late and then told me she wouldn’t discuss it further because I had yelled. AITA here??

prediction.raw:
I would say 1 (YTA - You're The Asshole). 

While it's understandable that you're upset about the situation, yelling at your wife and making her cry is not an acceptable way to handle the situation, especially when she's still recovering from childbirth. It's also important to consider that your wife was likely under a lot of stress and pressure during labor, and may have made the decision to call her mother out of emotional need or comfort.

Additionally, it's not entirely fair to blame your wife for "violating the plan" when you were late to the hospital, which may have contributed to her feeling anxious or alone. It's possible that she felt like she needed her mother's support during that time, and it's not necessarily about you or your feelings.

It's also worth considering that the birth of a child is a significant life event, and it's not just about the two of you having a "special one on one time" with the baby. It's about the arrival of a new family member, and it's natural that your wife may have wanted her mother to be a part of that experience.

A more constructive approach would be to have a calm and respectful conversation with your wife about your feelings and concerns, and to try to understand her perspective and why she made the decision to call her mother. Yelling and blaming her is unlikely to resolve the issue or improve your relationship.
